questions.stem: Many banyan trees have thick roots that grow from their branches towards the ground. What are these roots called?
options: Climbing stems
Flower stalks
Storage roots
Aerial roots

explain.why: Climbing stems are stems that wind around a support. These are roots, not stems.
Flower stalks hold up flowers. These hanging parts are roots.
Storage roots are thick roots under the ground, like a carrot, that store food.

solution: Roots that grow in the air are called aerial roots.

figure.alt: A banyan tree with a thick trunk, spreading branches and roots hanging from the branches.

questions.stem: A banyan tree has thick roots hanging from its branches (part B). How do these roots help the tree?
options: They attract insects to the flowers of the tree
They reach the ground and help to hold up the very heavy tree
They protect the seeds as they grow in the fruit
They make food for the whole tree using light and water

explain.why: Insects are attracted by the flowers, not by the roots.
Protecting seeds is the job of the fruit.
Food is made by the leaves (part C), not by the roots.

solution: Aerial roots that grow down into the ground help to support a large tree.

figure.alt: A banyan tree in line art with a thick trunk, spreading branches with leaves, and long roots hanging down from the branches, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: An orchid grows on the trunk of a tree. The roots labelled B hang in the air. Which statement about them is correct?
options: They hold up the leaves so they get sunlight
They grip the tree and take in moisture from the air
They take in water and mineral salts from the soil below the tree
They make the seeds that grow into new orchids

explain.why: Holding leaves up is a job of stems. These roots grip the tree.
The orchid sits on the trunk, not in soil. Its aerial roots take in moisture from the air.
Seeds are made by flowers, not by roots.

solution: Orchid aerial roots cling to the tree and take in moisture from the air.

figure.alt: An orchid growing on a tree trunk in line art, with a flower, leaves and long roots hanging in the air, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: A money plant has a weak stem. Small roots (part C) on its stem press against a pole. How does this help the plant?
options: The flowers of the plant open later in the night
The stem is held on the pole so the leaves can reach more light
The fruits grow larger on the plant and fall off sooner
The plant no longer needs its leaves to make food

explain.why: The small roots hold the stem on the pole. They do not change when flowers open.
The roots on the stem grip the pole. They do not make fruits larger.
All green plants still need leaves to make food.

solution: The small roots grip the pole so the weak stem climbs up towards the light.

figure.alt: A money plant climbing up a pole in line art, with heart-shaped leaves, a weak stem and small roots on the stem pressed against the pole, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: A pea plant has a weak stem. Its tendrils (part A) curl round a support. How does this help the plant?
options: The tendrils take in water from the moist air
The stem is held up so the leaves get light
The tendrils keep animals away from the plant
The tendrils make the seeds for the whole plant

explain.why: Tendrils hold on to a support. Water is taken in by the roots.
Keeping animals away is the job of thorns, not tendrils.
Seeds are made by the flower (part D), not the tendrils.

solution: Tendrils wind round a support and help the weak stem to climb.

figure.alt: A pea plant with a thin stem climbing a support in line art, with leaves, a flower and curly thread-like parts wound round the support, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: A cactus grows in a dry desert. How does the thick stem (part B) help it to live there?
options: It stores water for the dry times
It makes more leaves to lose water quickly
It attracts insects to the flowers
It lets the cactus float on water

explain.why: A cactus has spines, not leaves, so that it loses very little water.
Insects are attracted by the flower (part D), not by the stem.
A cactus does not live in water; its thick stem is a water store.

solution: The thick stem of a cactus holds water the plant can use when there is no rain.

figure.alt: A cactus in the desert in line art, shallow spreading roots and a flower, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: The stalk of a water lily (part B) has many air spaces. How does this help the plant?
options: It takes in more mineral salts from the mud below
It helps the leaf float to get sunlight
It stores seeds for when the pond dries up
It attracts more insects to the flower

explain.why: Mineral salts are taken in by the roots (part C) in the mud, not by the stalk.
The stalk does not store seeds. Its air spaces help the plant float.
Insects are attracted by the flower (part D), not by air spaces in the stalk.

solution: Air spaces make the stalk and leaf float so the leaf can get sunlight.

figure.alt: A water lily in a pond in line art, with a wide leaf floating on the surface, a long stalk, a flower and roots in the mud, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: Mangrove trees grow in soft mud. How do the thick, arching roots labelled B help the tree?
options: They hold the tree up firmly in mud
They take in air from the water around them
They carry the seeds of the tree to the mud
They make food for the tree

explain.why: The roots that stick up out of the mud (part A) help the tree get air. These arching roots hold it up.
Roots do not carry seeds. These roots hold the tree in the mud.
Food is made by the leaves (part C).

solution: Roots arching from the trunk spread out and hold the tree up in soft mud.

figure.alt: A mangrove tree in muddy water in line art, with curved roots arching from the trunk into the mud, short roots sticking up out of the mud, leaves and a trunk, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: Mangrove mud has very little air. Some roots (part A) grow upwards out of the mud. How does this help the tree?
options: They stop the tree from floating away
They let the roots get air
They attract insects to the flowers
They take in more sunlight for making food

explain.why: Holding the tree down is done by the arching roots (part B), not the roots sticking up.
Insects are attracted by flowers, not by roots.
Making food is done by the leaves (part C). Roots do not make food.

solution: Roots that stick up out of the mud take in air for the roots below.

figure.alt: A mangrove tree in muddy water in line art, with curved roots arching from the trunk into the mud, short roots sticking up out of the mud, leaves and a trunk, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: The thick orange part of a carrot is a root that stores food. Why is this useful to the carrot plant?
options: It lets the plant float on water
It protects the seeds of the carrot
It makes food for the plant using the sunlight under the soil
The plant can use the stored food later to grow

explain.why: A carrot plant grows in soil and a storage root does not help it float.
Seeds are protected by fruits. The carrot root holds food.
There is no sunlight under the soil, so it cannot make food there.

solution: A storage root keeps food that the plant can use later.

questions.stem: Kangkong grows floating in ponds. How does its hollow stem (part B) help it?
options: The hollow stem makes food for the roots below
The hollow stem takes in water from the pond
The water inside the stem makes the plant sink down
The air inside helps it to float

explain.why: Food is made by the leaves (part A).
Water is taken in by the roots (part C).
The air in the hollow stem makes the plant float, not sink.

solution: A hollow stem is full of air, which helps the kangkong float.

figure.alt: A kangkong plant floating in water in line art, with leaves, a long hollow stem and roots hanging in the water, with three marked positions.

questions.stem: Which feature best helps a plant to live in a very dry place?
options: A thick stem that stores water, and sharp spines
Long roots that hang in the air
Hollow stems full of air
Wide, thin leaves with a great many stomata

explain.why: Hanging aerial roots take moisture from damp air and would not help in a dry place.
Hollow stems full of air help plants float in water, not live in dry places.
Wide leaves with many stomata would lose too much water in a dry place.

solution: A plant in a dry place needs to save water.
A thick stem stores water. Spines lose very little.

questions.stem: A plant on the dark floor of a rainforest has large, thin leaves. How does this help it?
options: The leaves can catch more of the weak light
The leaves can lose less water vapour to the air
The leaves can hold the plant in the soil
The leaves can store more water

explain.why: A large, thin leaf has more surface and so loses more water, not less.
Holding the plant in the soil is done by the roots.
Thin leaves cannot store much water.

solution: A large leaf surface catches more of the weak light.

questions.stem: A tree on a windy seashore has strong roots that spread wide and deep. How does this help the tree?
options: The roots grip the soil so wind cannot blow it over
The roots help the leaves to float in the air above the tree
The roots attract insects to the flowers
The roots make food from the sunlight

explain.why: Leaves do not float in the air, and roots do not lift them.
Insects are attracted by flowers, not by roots.
Food is made by the leaves. Roots get no sunlight.

solution: Strong, spreading roots hold the tree firmly so it is not blown over.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of both the hanging roots of a banyan tree and the aerial roots of an orchid?
options: They hold the plant in the soil under it
They make the seeds of the plant
They make food using sunlight
They grow out in the air, above the ground

explain.why: An orchid on a tree trunk does not grow in soil.
Seeds are made by flowers.
Food is made mainly by leaves, not by these roots.

solution: Aerial roots grow in the air.
Banyan roots hang from the branches and orchid roots hang from the tree they grow on.

questions.stem: A cactus grows in a hot, dry desert. Which part of the cactus stores water?
options: The thick stem
The tiny roots only
The flowers
The sharp spines

explain.why: Roots take water in. The water is stored in the thick stem.
Flowers help the plant to make seeds, not store water.
Spines are thin and cannot hold water.

solution: The thick stem of a cactus stores water for the dry times.

figure.alt: A cactus growing in the desert.

questions.stem: The leaves of a cactus are thin, sharp spines. How does this help the cactus live in a desert?
options: It takes in more water from the air
Less water is lost from the plant
It makes the stem grow taller
More light is caught for making food

explain.why: Spines do not take in water.
Spines have nothing to do with height.
Wide leaves, not spines, catch more light.

solution: Small spines have very little surface, so very little water vapour escapes.

figure.alt: A cactus growing in the desert.

questions.stem: Some roots of a mangrove tree grow upwards out of the muddy water. Why does the tree have these roots?
options: To make seeds
To catch sunlight
To take in air
To take in more mud

explain.why: Seeds are not made in roots.
Roots do not catch light. Leaves do.
The tree does not need to take in mud.

solution: Mud has very little air. Roots growing up into the air can take it in.

figure.alt: A mangrove tree in muddy water, with curved roots arching from the trunk and some roots growing up out of the mud.

questions.stem: A water lily has wide leaves that float on the water. How does this help the plant?
options: The leaves can take in water from the soil
The leaves can catch lots of sunlight
The leaves can hold the plant in the mud
The leaves can store air for the roots

explain.why: Leaves are not the part that takes in water from the soil.
Roots hold a plant in the mud, not floating leaves.
Storing air is not the job of wide leaves.

solution: Floating leaves lie in the light, so they can make food.

figure.alt: A water lily in a pond, with a wide leaf floating on the surface.

questions.stem: A fish has a smooth body that is narrow at the front and the back. How does this help the fish?
options: It can move through water easily
It can hide among rocks on land
It can breathe air easily
It can stay on land for a long time

explain.why: A fish lives in water, so this does not help.
A fish breathes with its gills. Its shape does not help it breathe air.
A fish cannot live on land.

solution: A smooth, narrow body makes less push from the water, so the fish swims fast.

questions.stem: A camel has a hump that stores fat. How does this help the camel in the desert?
options: It stops the camel from sweating
It helps the camel to float
It is a store of food for hard times
It keeps the camel cool in the shade

explain.why: The fat does not stop sweating.
A camel does not live in water.
The hump is a food store, not a cooler.

solution: Fat in the hump can be used as food when there is little to eat.

questions.stem: A polar bear has thick fur and a thick layer of fat under its skin. How does this help it?
options: It keeps the bear warm in the cold
It helps the bear to hide in the desert
It helps the bear to run fast
It lets the bear store water

explain.why: Polar bears live in cold places, not deserts.
Fur and fat do not make it faster.
Fat and fur keep in heat. They are not for storing water.

solution: Thick fur and fat keep heat in, so the bear stays warm.

questions.stem: A tortoise pulls its head and legs into its hard shell when it is in danger. How does the shell help it?
options: It keeps the tortoise cool in the sun
It helps the tortoise to swim fast
It helps the tortoise to find food
It protects the tortoise from enemies

explain.why: The shell is for protection.
A heavy shell does not make it swim fast.
A shell does not help find food.

solution: A hard shell is hard for enemies to bite or crush, so the tortoise is safer.

questions.stem: A duck has webbed feet. How do they help the duck?
options: They help the duck to dig for worms
They help the duck to climb trees
They push the water to help it swim
They keep the duck warm in the nest

explain.why: Webbed feet are for swimming, not digging.
Webbed feet are not good for climbing.
Webbing on the feet is for swimming.

solution: The skin between the toes makes the foot wide, so it pushes more water.

questions.stem: Many birds fly to a warmer place when the cold season begins. What kind of adaptation is this?
options: A structural adaptation
A behavioural adaptation
A food-making adaptation
A seed dispersal adaptation

explain.why: A structural adaptation is a body part. Flying away is an action the bird does.
The birds do not make food. They move to find food and warmth.
Seed dispersal is about plants. Birds are moving themselves.

solution: Moving to another place is something the animal does, so it is behavioural.

questions.stem: Which of these is a structural adaptation?
options: A porcupine's sharp quills
A bird flying to a warmer place
A bear sleeping through the cold season
A squirrel storing nuts

explain.why: This is something the bird does, so it is behavioural.
This is behaviour, not a body part.
This is behaviour, not a body part.

solution: A structural adaptation is a part of the body, such as quills.
The other three are things animals do.

questions.stem: A seed has a thin, light wing. How does the wing help the plant?
options: It helps the seed to take in water
It helps the seed to float on a pond
It sticks the seed to an animal's fur
The wind can carry the seed far away

explain.why: The wing is not for taking in water.
The thin wing is for the wind, not water.
Sticking to fur needs hooks or sticky parts, not a wing.

solution: A light wing catches the wind, so seeds travel away from the parent plant.

questions.stem: A coconut has a thick husk that holds air. How does this help the coconut plant?
options: It lets the wind carry the coconut
It can float to faraway places
It makes animals eat the coconut
It keeps the coconut warm

explain.why: A coconut is too heavy to be carried by wind.
The husk is not a food for animals.
The husk is for floating.

solution: The husk holds air and floats, so water carries the coconut away from the tree.

questions.stem: A seed has many tiny hooks on its outside. How does this help the plant?
options: It can be blown by the wind
It can cling to an animal
It can make food for the plant
It can float on water

explain.why: Hooks do not help a seed travel by wind.
Hooks do not make food.
Hooks do not help a seed float.

solution: Hooks catch on fur or clothes, so the seed is carried to a new place.

questions.stem: A forest is cut down to build a road. What happens to many of the animals that lived there?
options: They lose their homes
They grow thicker fur
They find more food and shelter
They are not affected

explain.why: Animals cannot change their bodies that quickly.
Fewer trees means less food and shelter.
Their habitat is gone, so they are affected.

solution: Trees give food and shelter. When they are cut down, animals lose their homes.

questions.stem: Which of these actions is good for the environment?
options: Burning rubbish in an open field
Pouring used cooking oil down the drain
Planting new trees in a cleared area
Throwing plastic bags into the sea

explain.why: Burning rubbish puts smoke and harmful gases in the air.
Oil pollutes the water and harms animals and plants.
Plastic harms sea animals and does not break down quickly.

solution: New trees give food and shelter and help to replace what was lost.

questions.stem: Why is it harmful to pour oil into the sea?
options: It makes the sea cooler
It gives sea animals more food
It makes the water cleaner
It harms sea animals and plants

explain.why: Oil does not make the sea cooler.
Oil is not food. It covers and poisons animals.
Oil makes water dirty, not clean.

solution: Oil covers the water. It poisons the animals and plants that live in it.

questions.stem: Recycling paper helps the environment because fewer ____ need to be cut down.
options: rocks
clouds
trees
fish

explain.why: Paper is made from trees, not rocks.
Paper is not made from clouds.
Paper is not made from fish.

solution: Paper is made from wood.
Recycling used paper means fewer trees are cut down.

questions.stem: Burning large amounts of fuel puts gases in the air that make the Earth warmer. This is called ____.
options: deforestation
recycling
global warming
reforestation

explain.why: Deforestation is the cutting down of forests.
Recycling means using materials again.
Reforestation means planting trees again.

solution: The Earth getting warmer because of gases from burning fuel is called global warming.

questions.stem: A student brings her own bag when she goes shopping instead of taking new plastic bags. How does this help the environment?
options: More forest is cleared for roads
More trees are cut down
Less plastic rubbish is made
More oil is poured into the sea

explain.why: Her own bag does not clear forests.
A cloth bag does not need more trees to be cut.
This has nothing to do with using her own bag.

solution: Using a bag again means fewer new plastic bags are made and thrown away.

questions.stem: An owl has very large eyes that can see well in dim light. How does this help it?
options: It can hide in the sand
It can store water for a long time
It can hunt at night
It can swim very fast

explain.why: Large eyes do not help an owl hide in sand.
Eyes do not store water.
Eyes do not help an owl swim.

solution: Large eyes let an owl see in the dark, so it can look for food at night.

questions.stem: A frog has green and brown skin that looks like the plants around it. How does this help the frog?
options: It stores food for the frog
It helps the frog swim faster
It keeps the frog warm at night
Enemies find it hard to see the frog

explain.why: Skin colour is not a food store.
Skin colour does not make a frog swim faster.
Skin colour does not keep a frog warm.

solution: Skin that matches the plants helps the frog hide from its enemies.

questions.stem: A mole has strong front legs with large claws. How do they help the mole?
options: It can swim across ponds
It can fly short distances
It can climb tall trees
It can dig tunnels in the soil

explain.why: Strong claws are not for swimming.
A mole cannot fly.
A mole lives under the ground, not in trees.

solution: Strong legs and large claws are good for digging, so a mole can make tunnels.

questions.stem: A giraffe has a very long neck. How does this help it?
options: It can reach leaves high up on trees
It can dig for roots in the ground
It can hide in the long grass
It can swim in deep water

explain.why: A long neck is not for digging.
A tall animal cannot hide easily in grass.
A long neck does not help a giraffe swim.

solution: A long neck lets a giraffe reach food that other animals cannot reach.

questions.stem: The table shows four animals and a body feature of each. Which animal is best suited to live in a very cold place?
options: Q
P
S
R

explain.why: P has a thin, bare skin that loses body heat quickly, so it suits a warm place.
S has a thin coat of short hairs, which would not keep it warm in the cold.
R has large, thin ears used to lose heat, which suits a hot place.

solution: A thick layer of fat and thick fur keep heat in.
So Q can live in a very cold place.

questions.stem: The table shows the leaves of four plants. Which plant is most likely to survive in a hot, dry place?
options: S
T
V
U

explain.why: S has big, thin leaves that lose a lot of water to the air.
V grows its leaves under water, so it does not live in a dry place.
U has thin leaves with many openings, which lose water quickly in the heat.

solution: Small leaves with a thick waxy coat lose very little water.
Plant T is the one that can survive in a dry place.

questions.stem: The table shows the feet of four animals. Which animal spends most of its time swimming in water?
options: P
S
R
Q

explain.why: P has long toes that grip branches, so it lives in trees.
R has sharp claws for digging or catching prey on land.
Q has hard hooves for running on hard ground.

solution: Webbed feet push against a lot of water, so S swims well.

questions.stem: A stick insect looks like a twig of the plant it lives on. How does this help the stick insect?
options: It can fly higher than other insects
Predators find it hard to see it
It stays warm in the cold season
It can catch other insects more easily

explain.why: Its shape does not help it fly. It helps it hide.
A twig-like shape does not keep it warm.
Looking like a twig hides the insect from predators. It is not for hunting.

solution: Looking like a twig is camouflage. Predators do not notice the insect, so fewer of them eat it.

questions.stem: Which row correctly shows a structural adaptation and a behavioural adaptation?
options: A bear sleeping through winter; thick fur of a bear
A bird flying to a warmer place in winter; a bear sleeping through winter
Thick fur of a bear; webbed feet of a duck
Webbed feet of a duck; a bird flying to a warmer place in winter

explain.why: The order is the wrong way round. Sleeping is behavioural and thick fur is structural.
Both are things animals do, so both are behavioural. None of them is a body part.
Both are body parts, so both are structural. None of them is something the animal does.

solution: A structural adaptation is a body part or body covering, such as webbed feet.
A behavioural adaptation is what the animal does, such as flying to a warmer place.

questions.stem: Many birds fly to another country when winter comes. What is the main reason this helps them to survive?
options: They need to grow thicker feathers
They can find more food in the warmer place
They can lay more eggs in the cold place
They want to be away from the sunlight

explain.why: Flying away is not how they grow feathers.
Food is hard to find in winter. Laying eggs in the cold is not the reason.
Birds do not need to escape sunlight in winter.

solution: In winter the cold place has little food.
Birds that fly to a warmer place can find food and survive.

questions.stem: Many desert animals hide in burrows during the day and come out only at night. How does this help them survive?
options: They can stay warm during the cold days
They can see better in the strong sunlight
They can eat the plants that only grow at night
They avoid the heat of the day and lose less water

explain.why: Desert days are hot, not cold.
At night there is no strong sunlight.
Plants do not grow only at night. The reason is the heat.

solution: Days in the desert are very hot. Staying in a burrow keeps the animal cool.
It also loses less water from its body.

questions.stem: A bear eats a lot in autumn and then sleeps in a cave through winter, living off the fat it stored. How does this help the bear?
options: It keeps the bear safe from the heat
It lets the bear hunt in the dark
It saves energy when there is little food
It makes the bear grow bigger in winter

explain.why: Winter is the cold season, so heat is not the problem.
The bear is asleep and does not hunt.
The bear uses up fat in winter and does not grow.

solution: Food is scarce in winter. Sleeping uses very little energy, so the stored fat lasts until spring.

questions.stem: A rabbit has an eye on each side of its head. How does this help the rabbit?
options: It can judge the distance to its food exactly
It can see in the dark
It can see a wide area and spot danger
It can see small insects very clearly

explain.why: Judging distance well needs both eyes at the front, like a hunter.
The position of the eyes does not help seeing in the dark.
Eyes on the sides give a wide view, not a close, sharp one.

solution: Eyes on the sides of the head let a rabbit see almost all around it.
It can spot a predator coming from any direction.

questions.stem: The leaves of a cactus are covered by a thick waxy layer. How does this help the plant?
options: It helps the roots take in water
It lets more sunlight reach the leaves
It makes the leaves taste bad to insects
It stops water from escaping from the leaves

explain.why: The waxy layer is on the leaves, not the roots.
A thick layer cuts down water loss. It does not let in more light.
The waxy layer does not stop insects. It keeps water in.

solution: A thick waxy layer is waterproof. Water cannot escape from the cactus into the dry air.

questions.stem: The graph shows the area of forest in a country over 40 years. Which statement is correct?
options: The area of forest became bigger every 10 years
The area of forest was smallest in 1980
The area of forest stayed the same
The area of forest became smaller every 10 years

explain.why: The line goes down. The area gets smaller.
1980 had the largest area. The smallest was in 2020.
The values are lower at each point on the graph.

solution: Each point on the line is lower than the one before.
So the forest became smaller every 10 years.

questions.stem: Trees are planted on a bare hillside. How does this help the environment?
options: Their roots hold the soil so it is not washed away by rain
Their leaves make the rain fall faster onto the hill
Their flowers make the soil warmer for the plants
Their roots make the soil too hard to be washed away

explain.why: Trees do not make rain fall faster.
Flowers do not warm the soil.
Roots do not harden the soil. They hold it in place.

solution: Roots of trees hold the soil together.
This stops heavy rain from washing the soil down the hill.

questions.stem: Fishermen catch too many fish, including young ones, from a sea each year. After some years, there are very few fish. What is the best reason?
options: The sea water became too salty
Too few fish were left to breed and make young
The young fish grew bigger and ate each other
The fish moved to a warmer sea

explain.why: Catching fish does not change how salty the sea is.
The young fish were being caught before they could grow.
Fish do not all leave because of fishing. The fish were caught.

solution: Catching too many fish, young ones too, leaves too few to breed.
So the number of fish keeps falling.

questions.stem: Why does recycling aluminium cans help the environment?
options: Less metal has to be mined from the ground
The cans make the soil more fertile
The cans give off less heat when they rot
More cans can be thrown into the sea

explain.why: Cans do not add anything good to soil.
Metal cans do not rot. Recycling saves resources.
Throwing cans into the sea pollutes it. Recycling means the cans are used again.

solution: Recycling uses old cans to make new ones.
So less metal needs to be dug up, which saves natural resources.

questions.stem: Penguins in a very cold place huddle close together in groups. How does this help them?
options: They lose less body heat
They can see danger from further away
They can swim faster
They can catch more fish

explain.why: Standing together does not help them see further.
Huddling happens on the ice, not in the water.
Penguins huddle to keep warm, not to catch fish.

solution: Huddling together keeps the warm air between their bodies, so each penguin loses less heat.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a behavioural adaptation that helps an animal escape from predators?
options: A porcupine has sharp quills on its back
A stick insect has a body shaped like a twig
A hedgehog curls into a ball when it is frightened
A frog has green skin like the leaves around it

explain.why: Quills are body parts, so this is a structural adaptation.
This is a body shape, so it is a structural adaptation.
Skin colour is part of the body, so it is structural.

solution: A behavioural adaptation is something an animal does.
Curling into a ball is what the hedgehog does when in danger.

questions.stem: Which row correctly matches each animal to how its feature helps it survive?
options: Camel: large hump, so it stores water
Polar bear: thin fur, so it can swim faster
Duck: sharp claws, so it can push through water
Camel: wide flat feet, so it does not sink into sand

explain.why: The hump stores fat, not water.
A polar bear has thick fur to keep warm.
A duck has webbed feet for swimming, not sharp claws.

solution: Wide, flat feet spread the camel's weight over a larger area, so it does not sink into soft sand.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are structural adaptations?
A: A frog's green skin.
B: A bear's winter sleep.
C: A fish's gills.
D: A swallow flying to a warm place in winter.
options: A and B only
A and C only
C and D only
B and D only

explain.why: B is something the bear does, so it is behavioural.
D is behavioural because it is something the bird does.
Both are things animals do, so both are behavioural.

solution: Skin colour and gills are parts of the body, so A and C are structural.
Sleeping through winter and flying away are behaviours.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are behavioural adaptations?
A: A cactus storing water in its stem.
B: A whale's thick layer of blubber.
C: A squirrel burying nuts in autumn.
D: A fish swimming in a group (school).
options: A and C only
B and D only
C and D only
A and B only

explain.why: A is the stem of a plant, which is structural.
B is a body part, so it is structural.
Both are parts of the body, so both are structural.

solution: Burying nuts and swimming in a group are things the animals do, so they are behavioural.
A and B are body parts.

questions.stem: The table shows the leaves and roots of two plants, A and B. Where does each plant most likely live?
options: A lives on a dark rainforest floor and B lives in a desert
A lives in a desert and B lives on a dark rainforest floor
Both A and B live in a desert
Both A and B live on a dark rainforest floor

explain.why: Plant A, with small waxy leaves and deep roots, is the desert one.
Plant B has large thin leaves that would lose too much water in the heat.
Plant A has small waxy leaves. It lives where water is short.

solution: Small waxy leaves and deep roots save and find water in dry places.
Large thin leaves catch weak light in a dark forest.

options: P
R
Q
S

explain.why: R has a rough, bumpy body that would slow it down in water.
Q has a wide, flat body and short limbs, which do not cut through water.
S has long legs and a thin body made for running on land.

solution: A smooth body that is narrow at the ends and has fins can move easily through water.

options: The number of cubs did not change as the ice melted
As the sea ice became smaller, more cubs were born
As the sea ice became smaller, fewer cubs were born
The area of sea ice became larger every 5 years

explain.why: The number of cubs fell from 60 to 20.
The number of cubs fell when the ice area fell.
The ice area was smaller at each year shown.

solution: Both columns go down together.
There were fewer cubs when there was less sea ice.

questions.stem: Wei Ling puts a thick coat of wax on one of two identical leaves and leaves the other bare. She leaves both in the sun and weighs them each day. The table shows her results. What can she conclude?
options: A waxy coat makes a leaf take in more water
A leaf without wax loses water more slowly
Leaves lose no water when they are in the sun
A waxy coat helps a leaf lose less water

explain.why: The waxy leaf lost less mass, so it kept more water. It did not take any in.
The leaf without wax lost more mass, so it lost water faster.
Both leaves lost mass, so both lost water.

solution: The bare leaf's mass fell by 4 g. The waxy leaf's mass fell by only 1 g.
So the wax stops some water from escaping.

questions.stem: Paper moths of two colours were placed on a dark tree trunk. Birds were allowed to look for them for 10 minutes. The table shows how many were found. What can be concluded?
options: Birds only eat the pale moths that they find
Pale moths hide better on a dark trunk
Dark moths are always safer than pale moths everywhere
Moths that match their background are seen less

explain.why: Birds found some dark moths too, only fewer.
The pale moths were found more often on the dark trunk.
They were safer only on the dark trunk. On a pale background it may be the other way round.

solution: More pale moths were found on the dark trunk than dark moths.
So moths that match their background are seen less.

questions.stem: Oil spills from a ship into the sea and covers the feathers of seabirds. Why are these birds likely to die?
options: The oil makes their wings grow too large
Their feathers no longer keep them warm and dry
The oil gives them too much extra food to eat
The oil makes the sea water too salty to swim in

explain.why: Oil does not make wings grow.
Oil is not food. It harms the birds.
The harm comes from the oil on the feathers, not from salty water.

solution: Oil clogs the feathers, so water gets through to the skin.
The birds get cold and cannot swim or fly well.

questions.stem:
Which of the following actions can help to reduce global warming?
A: Planting more trees.
B: Burning more fuel in cars.
C: Using public transport.
D: Cutting down forests.
options: C and D only
A and C only
A and B only
B and D only

explain.why: D removes trees that take in carbon dioxide.
B puts more carbon dioxide into the air, which makes global warming worse.
Both make global warming worse.

solution: Trees take in carbon dioxide, and public transport burns less fuel for each person.
Burning more fuel and cutting forests make it worse.

questions.stem: After all the trees on a hillside are cut down, heavy rain washes soil into a river and the river water turns muddy. Why do the water plants in the river die?
options: The mud blocks light so they cannot make food
The mud gives them too many minerals to take in
The rain makes the river water too cold
The mud stops them from making flowers

explain.why: Mud in the water does not feed them. It blocks the light.
The rain is not the direct cause. It is the mud in the water.
The plants die because they cannot make food, not because of flowers.

solution: Muddy water lets in less light.
Plants need light to make food, so the water plants die.

questions.stem: A factory pours waste into a stream at point Q. The bar graph shows the number of fish at four points along the stream. P is before Q. Which statement is the best explanation of the graph?
options: The waste makes the fish grow bigger at point R
The waste harms fish near where it enters and is spread out further downstream
Fish prefer to live near the factory
There were fewer fish at point P because the stream began there

explain.why: The graph shows the number of fish, not their size. There are few at R.
Very few fish live near the factory outlet.
P had the most fish. It is before the waste.

solution: Point P is before the waste and has many fish.
Point Q is at the outlet and has the fewest. The number grows again as the waste is diluted.

questions.stem: A desert fox has very large ears that have many blood vessels close to the skin. How do the large ears help the fox?
options: They keep the sand out of its eyes
They keep the fox's body warm in the cold desert night
They let the fox lose body heat to the air
They help the fox store water in its body

explain.why: Large ears are for losing heat, not for blocking sand.
Large thin ears lose heat. They would make the fox colder.
Ears do not store water.

solution: Heat moves out of the blood into the air through the large, thin ears.
This helps the fox stay cool in the hot desert.

questions.stem: The graph shows the average temperature of the Earth over 40 years. Which statement is correct?
options: The average temperature was highest in 1980
The average temperature stayed the same
The average temperature fell over the years
The average temperature rose over the years

explain.why: 1980 had the lowest value on the graph.
The values are higher each time.
The line goes up, so the temperature rose.

solution: Each point on the line is higher than the one before it, so the average temperature rose.

questions.stem: A farmer puts too much fertiliser on his field. Some of it washes into a nearby pond, and green algae spread over the surface. Why may the fish in the pond die?
options: The algae give off a gas that helps fish to breathe
The algae use up all the food of the fish in one day
The fertiliser makes the pond water too cold for the fish
Algae block light, so plants die and oxygen is used up

explain.why: Dying plants and algae use up oxygen, they do not add it for the fish.
Fish are not killed that fast by the algae eating their food. The main problem is the light and oxygen.
Fertiliser does not change the water temperature much.

solution: Algae cover the surface and cut off light, so the plants below die.
Dead plants rot and use oxygen, and the fish do not have enough to breathe.

questions.stem: Which shows the correct chain of events that leads to global warming?
options: More fuel burnt, less carbon dioxide in the air, more heat trapped, Earth becomes warmer
More fuel burnt, more carbon dioxide in the air, more heat trapped, Earth becomes warmer
More trees planted, more carbon dioxide in the air, more heat trapped, Earth becomes warmer
More fuel burnt, more carbon dioxide in the air, less heat trapped, Earth becomes cooler

explain.why: Burning fuel gives more carbon dioxide, not less.
More trees take in carbon dioxide, so there would be less of it.
More carbon dioxide traps more heat and the Earth warms.

solution: Burning fuel adds carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide traps heat, so the Earth becomes warmer.

questions.stem: A camel has a hump of fat on its back. Which statement is correct about how the hump helps the camel?
options: The hump holds a large store of water for the camel
The hump keeps the camel's body cool in the sun
The hump makes the camel run faster over the sand
The fat can be used for energy when the camel cannot find food

explain.why: The hump holds fat. It does not hold water.
Fat on the back does not cool the camel.
The hump has no effect on how fast it runs.

solution: The hump stores fat, which the camel's body breaks down to get energy when food is scarce.

questions.stem:
Which statements about reducing waste are correct?
A: Washing and reusing glass jars saves resources.
B: Throwing away things that can be mended reduces waste.
C: Sorting paper and bottles for recycling means less new material is needed.
D: Using a lot of plastic bags gives less rubbish.
options: A and C only
C and D only
B and D only
A and B only

explain.why: D is wrong. Using many plastic bags makes more rubbish.
Both B and D increase waste.
B is wrong. Throwing away things that can be mended makes more waste.

solution: Reusing jars and recycling save resources, so A and C are correct.
B and D make more rubbish.

questions.stem: An Arctic fox has brown fur in summer and white fur in winter. How does this help the fox?
options: It lets the fox store more fat for winter
Other animals find it hard to see it on the ground
It keeps the fox warm during the summer months
It makes the fox's fur grow faster in each season

explain.why: Fur colour has nothing to do with storing fat.
Brown fur does not warm the fox. The colour helps it hide.
Fur colour does not change how fast fur grows.

solution: The fur colour matches the ground in each season.
That makes the fox hard to see, so it can hide from predators and sneak up on prey.

questions.stem: Why is it a good idea for a country to have rules to stop people from hunting rare animals?
options: The animals can breed and their numbers can grow again
The animals will move to another country
The rare animals will become fiercer
There will be fewer plants for them to eat

explain.why: The rules do not make animals move. They protect those in the country.
Rules do not change how fierce animals are.
Plants are not affected this way. The rules protect the animals.

solution: If the animals are not hunted, more of them live to breed.
Their numbers can grow again and the kind is not lost.

questions.stem: The table shows four animals that live in a hot desert. Which animal is best adapted to survive there?
options: S
Q
P
R

explain.why: S is active at night, but its thin fur and small ears do not help it lose heat or save water.
Q has a thin, bare body that loses water quickly and is active in the day.
P has thick fur and is active in the day, so it would overheat.

solution: R has large ears to lose heat, a waxy skin that holds in water, and it is active at night when it is cool.
